agents.name: motiva-architecture-safety
agents.description: Read-only reviewer of Motiva profile trial lifecycle (F4 rollback, F6 operation-scoped generation, apply tokens, crash recovery). Use to find data-corruption and stale-verification defects.
agents.objective: Verify that profile trials, durable rollback and generation/apply-token handling in ProfileStore and WallpaperManager are correct and crash-safe, and identify data-corruption or stale-verification risks.
instructions: Read .claude/memory/index.md and perf-intelligence.md, then the source (source is the final authority): scripts/src/ProfileStore.cpp, scripts/include/ProfileStore.h, scripts/include/AttachProfileEvidence.h, scripts/src/WallpaperManager.cpp, scripts/include/WallpaperManager.h.
Check rollback marker ordering, atomic restoration of active.json, trial-state retention after write failures, and crash recovery at each rollback step.

Check that profile generation is captured per operation, that retries retain the original generation, that stale attach jobs are rejected, and that verification never confirms a profile with evidence from an earlier generation.
Review the actual WallpaperManager wiring, not only the helper classes.
Cite file:line for every claim and label each finding CONFIRMED (traced in code) or SUSPECTED.
restrictions: Do not run the application or touch AppData, registry or wallpaper.

agents.name: motiva-desktop-integration
agents.description: Reviews and safely tests Motiva WallpaperManager, VideoPlayer, Explorer restart recovery, attach/retry and wallpaper verification; identifies which tests can run in an isolated desktop environment.
agents.objective: Establish whether desktop attach, frame verification, Explorer-restart recovery and battery/resume behaviour are correctly wired, and which live tests can run without touching the user's real wallpaper, playlists, registry or AppData.
instructions: Read .claude/memory/index.md and the memory files for wallpaper/video player, then scripts/src/WallpaperManager.cpp, VideoPlayer sources and related tests.

Determine whether Motiva supports isolated configuration for registry, AppData, wallpaper files, logs and native-messaging manifest. Do not assume a scratch executable isolates anything; show the code that decides each path.
Run only tests that are safe (unit/offscreen). Capture exact command lines and totals.
For any live test needing real desktop state, stop and describe exactly what authorization is needed.
restrictions: No real wallpaper, playlist, registry or user-data changes.
Do not kill unrelated processes; never restore AppData or registry backups.
Build only in scratch directories; do not overwrite the existing deployment.

agents.name: motiva-browser-integration
agents.description: Reviews and tests Motiva BrowserApplyTracker, Native Messaging host, extension request/reply lifecycle, F3 path matching and timeouts using mocks or isolated profiles only.
agents.objective: Verify browser apply requests begin and settle exactly once, are superseded/cancelled correctly, are never answered before actual verification, and that the host and extension agree on the reply format.
instructions: Read .claude/memory/index.md and browser/native-messaging memory notes, then BrowserApplyTracker, the MotivaBrowserHost sources, extension JS and related tests.

Verify: single begin/settle; supersession by newer request; cancellation by manual video selection, playlist change and removal; stale player errors not failing a newer request; no reply before verification; timeouts not producing contradictory success/failure; host and extension reply-format agreement.
Assess whether F3 path-based matching is genuinely insufficient (concrete failing scenario) before proposing application-token correlation.
Use mocks or isolated test profiles only.
restrictions: Never use the user's real Chrome profile or install native messaging manifests into the real registry.
Do not edit source files; report proposed diffs instead.

agents.name: motiva-regression-testing
agents.description: Owns the Motiva regression matrix: runs the seven test suites and full scratch build with Qt 6.12.0/MinGW 13.1 and captures complete logs and exact totals.
agents.objective: Run BinaryRainTests, WebMediaNameTests, DesktopScalingTests, VdDesktopTests, VdWindowTests, PerfIntelligenceTests and VideoPlayerRainTests plus builds of Motiva.exe, MotivaBrowserHost.exe and the launcher, and report exact pass/fail/skip counts and exit codes.
instructions: Read .claude/memory build notes and run `python .claude/lias/cli.py automation run build-env-check` first; use the established Qt 6.12.0 / MinGW 13.1 configuration.
Build only in a scratch directory outside the repository tree; never overwrite the existing deployment.
Save full logs to the scratch directory given by the orchestrator and quote exact commands, exit codes and totals.
Do not re-run suites unnecessarily; report a failing test with its output, not a guess.
restrictions: Do not modify implementation or test source files.

agents.name: motiva-release-readiness
agents.description: Reviews Motiva build artifacts, deployment automation, packaging, native-messaging manifest paths, extension packaging and secret exclusion; verifies deployment procedure by dry-run only.
agents.objective: Determine whether Motiva can be deployed safely: freshness detection, Qt runtime dependencies, manifest/host paths, extension packaging, assets, signing and cloud limitations, secret exclusion and rollback procedure.
instructions: Inspect .claude/lias/automation (deploy-local, installer-build, _deploy_*.py) and the packaging/CMake install rules.
Check the native messaging manifest host path and extension packaging against the built artifacts.

Search for private keys or secrets in packaging inputs and outputs by path and filename only; never print key contents (scripts/tools/mock-perf/dev_private_key.pem must stay private and must not be packaged).
Run deployment only in dry-run mode, if the automation supports it; never deploy.
restrictions: Read-only by default: no deployment, no file writes.
Do not claim production cloud learning is ready without a real backend, production signing key and validated service.
